# What the front ends said

Every warning every front end printed about every corpus case, with the number of cases it fired on and what it means. A warning is a statement, and it says one of three things — our case is ambiguous, the vendor deviates deliberately, or the specification leaves something open. All three are findings.

Measured by `tools/interop-results/warning-sweep.sh`, which runs each front end and **stops there**: no fill, no compile, no link, no run. It produces no bytes and changes none, so it is a separate measurement and not a re-record.

The severity is the one the diagnostic claims and never the one its exit status implies. The two contradict each other here: `tao_idl` prints `Error - …: fixed data types are not supported` and **exits 0**, on all ten `fixed` cases.

## What no cell here can say

A front end is not the only program a probe runs. Every probe in `tools/wireprobe` then compiles, and every one of them writes its compiler's output to a `cc.log` inside a `mktemp -d` that a `trap … EXIT` removes, reads back `error:` lines and reads them only when the build failed. `wireprobe-ros` compiles with `-w` and `wireprobe-jacorb` with `javac -nowarn`; `wireprobe-zerodds-c` compiles this project's own generated C with `-Werror`.

So a system with no row below is a system whose **front end** was quiet, and nothing more. The compiler stage has never been listened to, and the one warning that would have caught the `wchar` fill defect at its source — gcc's default `-Wmultichar` — was printed on every probe build that carried the literal and deleted with the directory it was printed into. `docs/compiler-diagnostics-followup.md` is the entry for it.

58 distinct warning texts over 555 case-and-system pairs. 5 of them change what a row of [`write.md`](write.md) says.

## What each of them means

### `cyclone` / `idlc` — 153 cases

> No default extensibility provided. For one or more of the aggregated types in the IDL the extensibility is not explicitly set. Currently the default extensibility for these types is 'final', but this may change to 'appendable' in a future release because that is the default in the DDS XTypes specification.

**deliberate deviation.** Cyclone's own statement that its answer to §7.3.1.2.1.8 is not the specification's. The clause makes an unannotated aggregate `appendable`; `idlc` makes it `final`, says so, and says it intends to change. It is the root cause of GitHub issues #41 and #42, and it is in no clause and in no byte. **It changes a verdict**: on 102 of the 115 of these cases where Cyclone and a peer both produced bytes, every peer's XCDR2 payload is longer than Cyclone's by a positive multiple of four — one DHEADER per defaulted aggregate — which is the H9 divergence measured from the other side. `docs/omg-xtypes-issues.md` §B6 is the draft comment.

Carried into [`docs/wire-feature-inventory.md`](../../docs/wire-feature-inventory.md) row **H9**.

### `opendds` / `tao_idl` — 148 cases

> Warning - tao_idl: "gen.idl", line L: error in lookup of symbol: final

**not implemented.** `tao_idl` 2.5.24 knows none of the XTypes annotations — `@final`, `@appendable`, `@mutable`, `@key`, `@id`, `@hashid`, `@optional`, `@external`, `@must_understand`. It parses each one, drops it, and exits 0, which is a fourth behaviour distinct from accepting, refusing and honouring. For the OpenDDS column it is the C++ *mapping* that loses them and `opendds_idl` that decides the wire, so most of these change nothing; `bit_bound` and `value` are the two that reach the octets and they have their own rows above.

Carried into [`docs/wire-feature-inventory.md`](../../docs/wire-feature-inventory.md) row **G15**.

### `opendds` / `opendds_idl` — 36 cases

> Warning - opendds_idl: "gen.idl", line L: error in lookup of symbol: bit_bound

**not implemented.** Neither of OpenDDS's two generators resolves `@bit_bound`. **It changes a verdict**: `enum-bitbound-8-plain` is three octets from Cyclone and from this project and nine from OpenDDS, because the enumeration keeps the 32-bit holder §7.3.1.2.1.5 lets `@bit_bound` narrow. The table recorded the difference; this is the sentence that says what caused it.

> gen.idl:L:C: Inheriting from appendable structs is unsafe

**unspecified by the standard.** Cyclone's reading of §7.2.2.4.4, which permits a struct to inherit from an `@appendable` base and does not say what a reader does with a base whose length grew. `idlc` generates the type support anyway and exits 0. ### `fastdds` / `fastddsgen` — 1 case

> [0.217s][warning][os,thread] Failed to start thread "Unknown thread" - pthread_create failed (EAGAIN) for attributes: stacksize: 1024k, guardsize: 0k, detached.

**about the measuring host, not the case.** **Not a statement about Fast DDS and not one about a case.** The JVM that runs `fastddsgen` could not create a thread: `[0.293s][warning][os,thread] Failed to start thread "Unknown thread" - pthread_create failed (EAGAIN)`, printed by HotSpot's own unified logging, on a run that then exited 1. `EAGAIN` from `pthread_create` is the host at its thread or process limit, and the sweep runs `--jobs N` generators at once, each a JVM. **Which measurement it belonged to, and what became of it.** The row is filed under the case `-`, and `probe_diagnostics_batch` in `tools/wireprobe/diagnostics.sh` files a line under `-` only when the chunk that produced it held **more than one** case — a chunk of one names its case on every line. A multi-case chunk whose generator fails and whose log blames no case is `return 9` in `tools/wireprobe/wireprobe-batch`'s `run_chunk`: the chunk is split and the halves are built again, and no cell is recorded from it. The 52 rows that say `fastddsgen failed and named no case` come from the other branch of that same function, which is reached only at one case remaining, and none of them carries a thread diagnostic — `EAGAIN`, `Failed to start thread`, `unable to create native thread` and `OutOfMemoryError` appear in `sources/` exactly once, here. **So no committed cell was measured under it**, and it is kept because the next one might not be as harmless: a verdict reached while the host was refusing threads is not a verdict about the vendor, and it has to be re-recorded rather than read.

Cases: [`-`](../interop-corpus/-/type.idl)

> [0.224s][warning][os,thread] Failed to start thread "Unknown thread" - pthread_create failed (EAGAIN) for attributes: stacksize: 1024k, guardsize: 0k, detached.

**about the measuring host, not the case.** **Not a statement about Fast DDS and not one about a case.** The JVM that runs `fastddsgen` could not create a thread: `[0.293s][warning][os,thread] Failed to start thread "Unknown thread" - pthread_create failed (EAGAIN)`, printed by HotSpot's own unified logging, on a run that then exited 1. `EAGAIN` from `pthread_create` is the host at its thread or process limit, and the sweep runs `--jobs N` generators at once, each a JVM. **Which measurement it belonged to, and what became of it.** The row is filed under the case `-`, and `probe_diagnostics_batch` in `tools/wireprobe/diagnostics.sh` files a line under `-` only when the chunk that produced it held **more than one** case — a chunk of one names its case on every line. A multi-case chunk whose generator fails and whose log blames no case is `return 9` in `tools/wireprobe/wireprobe-batch`'s `run_chunk`: the chunk is split and the halves are built again, and no cell is recorded from it. The 52 rows that say `fastddsgen failed and named no case` come from the other branch of that same function, which is reached only at one case remaining, and none of them carries a thread diagnostic — `EAGAIN`, `Failed to start thread`, `unable to create native thread` and `OutOfMemoryError` appear in `sources/` exactly once, here. **So no committed cell was measured under it**, and it is kept because the next one might not be as harmless: a verdict reached while the host was refusing threads is not a verdict about the vendor, and it has to be re-recorded rather than read.

Cases: [`-`](../interop-corpus/-/type.idl)

### `fastdds` / `fastddsgen` — 1 case

> no such attribute: parent

**not implemented.** `fastddsgen` on the same case. It resolves an annotation name by its last segment and then looks for a *parent* attribute it has not been given, so a scoped annotation name reaches its type builder as a shape it has no branch for. Like RTI's two lines this says nothing about the octets — the case produces none from either — and everything about which half of rule (218) each front end implements.

### `omniorb` / `cc` — 1 case

> gen.hh: warning: switch condition has boolean value [-Wswitch-bool]

**about the generated source, not the wire.** `omniidl -bcxx` gives a union over `boolean` a `switch` on a `CORBA::Boolean`, and gcc warns because a two-valued switch is usually a mistake. It is not one here: the C++ mapping makes the discriminant a `Boolean` and a `switch` over it is what the generated accessor is. **It changes no verdict.** omniORB, TAO and JacORB all write `union-discriminator-boolean` as `01` then the branch, which is what this project writes, and the only octets that differ are the three fill positions the ORB probes mark. Measured on the test host, gcc 14.2.0, on `union-discriminator-boolean-unannotated`: `gen.hh: warning: switch condition has boolean value [-Wswitch-bool]`. It reached the record only when the probe cache was rebuilt — the cache key had not carried the template, so every ORB build was a hit on an entry from before `diagnostics.sh`, which is the failure that mechanism's own header describes.

Cases: [`union-discriminator-boolean-unannotated`](../interop-corpus/union-discriminator-boolean-unannotated/type.idl)

### `opendds` / `cc` — 1 case

> genTypeSupportImpl.cpp: warning: control reaches end of non-void function [-Wreturn-type]

**a cascade, not a statement.** Printed after an error in the same function, not about a function that forgot its `return`. OpenDDS 3.34's FACE mapping (`opendds_idl -Lface`, the one its `fixed` goes through) gives an anonymous `sequence` or array member of a `fixed` typedef a type it never declares (`::Sample::_amounts_seq`, `::Sample::_items_forany`); the `gen_skip_over` call naming it does not parse, and gcc reports the function body it abandoned as one with no `return`. **It changes no verdict**: the same build's `error:` lines are what refuse `sequence-fixed` and `array-1d-fixed`. Measured on the test host, gcc 14.2.0, compiling `genTypeSupportImpl.cpp` for `sequence-fixed`: `error: '_amounts_seq' in 'struct Sample' does not name a type` and four `expected` errors at line 476, then `warning: no return statement in function returning non-void [-Wreturn-type]` at line 494.

Cases: [`-`](../interop-corpus/-/type.idl)

### `ros-cyclone` / `cc` — 1 case

> fill.inc: warning: integer constant is so large that it is unsigned

**about the generated source, not the wire.** gcc on `fill.inc`, in both ROS columns, on `integer-extremes` — **this harness's own emitted C and not a vendor's**. C has no literal for `INT64_MIN`: `-9223372036854775808LL` is a positive constant too large for `long long`, so the constant is given an unsigned type and the unary minus is applied to it. What reaches the field is then an implementation-defined conversion rather than the value the case declares. **It changed no verdict**: `integer-extremes` is `80ff0080 ffff0000 00000080 ffffffff 00000000 00000080 ffffffffffffffff` from both ROS type supports and byte for byte the same from Cyclone, Fast DDS, hdds and the C column, so the intended `i64_min` did arrive. It is classed here and not written off, because the reason it arrived is the compiler's choice and not the literal's meaning. `crates/wire-probe/src/fill.rs` had already spelled the value as `(-9223372036854775807LL - 1)`, the subtraction `<stdint.h>` uses; `fill_ros.rs` and `fill_cpp.rs` had not been given it and now are, so a re-record of the two ROS columns is where this warning stops being printed. Keyed by its text and not by a switch, unlike the entries in `COMPILER_CLASSIFICATION`: gcc prints this one unconditionally and names no `[-W…]`, so there is no switch to key it by.

Cases: [`integer-extremes`](../interop-corpus/integer-extremes/type.idl)

### `rti` / `rtiddsgen` — 1 case

> WARN com.rti.ndds.nddsgen.antlr.auto.IdlParser gen.idl line 3 Custom annotation mark will be ignored.

**not implemented.** `rtiddsgen` reads `@ann::mark(7)` and drops it. IDL 4.2 rule (218) makes an annotation's name a `<scoped_name>`, so a user annotation declared inside a module is applied by its scoped name and this one is well formed. The generator takes the syntax, says it is ignoring the annotation and exits — which is the parsed-and-dropped behaviour `tao_idl` has for the builtin annotations, on a user one. It changes no octet here: `mark` is a user annotation with no wire effect, and the row is a statement about the reach of the syntax rather than about the bytes.

Cases: [`annotation-scoped-name`](../interop-corpus/annotation-scoped-name/type.idl)

### `rti` / `rtiddsgen` — 1 case

> gen.idl line L:C no viable alternative at character ':'

**not implemented.** `rtiddsgen`'s parser stops at the `::` of `@::key` — the root-anchored form of rule (218)'s `<scoped_name>`, which rule (4) admits. The two RTI lines on `annotation-scoped-name` are one behaviour seen twice: it takes `@ann::mark`, ignores it, and cannot take `@::key` at all.

Cases: [`annotation-scoped-name`](../interop-corpus/annotation-scoped-name/type.idl)

## The front ends that said nothing

`tao`, `jacorb` ran over the whole corpus and printed no warning at all. That is a measurement and not an absence: each of them refuses cases the others accept, and each does it with an error and no advice. Where a vendor drops a construct in silence there is nothing here to read, which is the difference between OpenDDS — which names every annotation it could not resolve — and Fast DDS, which resolves `@bit_bound` no better and says nothing.
